profiles.name: Leroy4522
profiles.profile: This is a full-contact negotiation with the golf course, and the course keeps getting the better lawyer. The ball-striking is usually putting him in the wood chipper, and the short game hasn’t exactly been calling 911 either. Then every so often he flashes enough touch to briefly confuse everybody into thinking the bleeding stopped. It’s volatile golf with a nasty hook: when the irons go sideways, the whole card starts looking like it was filled out by a guy with a grudge and a sharpie.

profiles.name: derekldavis
profiles.profile: This bag lives in the bunker and apparently sends postcards from there. The driver is already doing dumb things, but the real issue is how often the recovery game turns into a hostage situation. There are just enough competent stretches to keep you from writing him off completely, which makes the whole thing more annoying than cleanly awful. When the contact gets loose, the round doesn’t merely wobble — it starts drinking in public.

profiles.name: TEV_11
profiles.profile: He can absolutely launch it, and then the approach game walks in wearing a fake mustache and ruins the whole plot. There’s enough tee-ball pop here to tease you, but the shot pattern from there is the kind of thing that makes a grown man stare at a yardage book like it personally insulted his mother. The short game has shown a pulse, which is more than this thing deserves sometimes, but the scoring engine is still mostly held together by hope and one decent swing at a time.
